Simultaneous

/sim-ul-TAY-nee-us/ — stress on TAY · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Simultaneous means happening at exactly the same time as something else.

These simultaneous recordings, made from widely separated points on Earth, allowed researchers to measure the flare from two angles at once.

Worked Example

Two cameras positioned miles apart captured the solar flare simultaneously, recording the exact moment from different angles at the same time.

Simultaneous is more precise than simply saying 'at the same time' because it emphasizes that the timing is absolutely exact and coordinated — the flare happens as one unified moment rather than separate events that merely occur close together.

How Simultaneous Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

concurrent

concurrent: overlapping in time, not exact-moment precise

synchronous

synchronous: deliberately coordinated timing, often in systems

coincident

coincident: same-time by chance, not by design

Antonyms

sequential

sequential: occurring one after another in order

staggered

staggered: deliberately spaced out at different times

How Strong Is It? — separate → consecutive → overlapping → simultaneous

separate vs. simultaneous

separate vs. simultaneous: Calling the two fire drills separate only tells you they were distinct events; simultaneous tells you the alarms in both buildings sounded at the exact same instant.

consecutive vs. simultaneous

consecutive vs. simultaneous: The stagehand raised the two curtains consecutively, one right after the other; a simultaneous cue would have lifted both at the very same second.

overlapping vs. simultaneous

overlapping vs. simultaneous: The two radio programs were overlapping, sharing a few minutes of airtime, but they were not simultaneous, since neither began nor ended at exactly the same moment.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — simul-

Root — simul-: at the same time

Suffix — -taneous

Suffix — -taneous: characterized by (an adjective ending English borrowed from words like spontaneous and instantaneous)

Put it together

Put it together: Simul- (at the same time) + -taneous (characterized by) builds the meaning literally: characterized by happening at the same time. English took the -taneous ending from words like spontaneous and instantaneous and attached it to simul in Medieval Latin. Similar and simulate look like close relatives of simul, but they come from a different Latin root — similis, meaning 'like, resembling'; the two roots are only distant cousins, sharing an older ancestor that meant 'one, together.'

Use the root in a new word: simulcast

Use the root in a new word: simulcast: When a big game is simulcast on radio and television, fans following either one hear the final whistle at the same time.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / technical

Simultaneous is the precise word when two or more events happen at exactly the same moment in perfect time coordination. For casual speech about things happening around the same time (but not necessarily exact), 'at the same time' or 'concurrent' often works better.
